Unit 1 of 10: What Psychology Studies

Key ideas

  • Psychology is the systematic study of mental processes, experiences and behaviour in different contexts.
  • Mental processes: remembering, learning, thinking, problem solving — activities of the mind we cannot see directly but infer from behaviour.
  • Experiences: subjective, private states — joy, pain, the feeling of being in love. They depend on the person and the situation.
  • Behaviours: responses or reactions we make — overt (seen by others, e.g. running) or covert (inside us, e.g. a racing heart, thinking).
  • Psychology uses scientific methods to study these, so its conclusions can be checked.

Worked examples

Example 1: Classify: (i) solving a puzzle in your head (ii) blushing (iii) feeling nervous before a test. Answer: (i) mental process; (ii) behaviour (covert/overt physiological response); (iii) experience.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) Which is an overt behaviour? (a) thinking (b) a faster heartbeat (c) waving to a friend (d) dreaming. Answer: (c).
  2. (1 mark) Define psychology. Answer: the systematic study of mental processes, experiences and behaviour.
  3. (2 marks) Distinguish overt and covert behaviour with examples. Answer: overt — can be seen by others, e.g. talking (1); covert — internal, e.g. muscle tension or thinking (1).
  4. (3 marks) Explain the three things psychology studies. Answer: mental processes such as memory and thinking (1); experiences — subjective inner states (1); behaviour — responses that can be overt or covert (1).
  5. (3 marks) Why are experiences difficult to study scientifically? Answer: they are private and subjective (1); they depend on the person and the context (1); they can only be reported by the person, so psychologists rely on self-reports and indirect measures (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Defining psychology as "study of the soul" only. 2. Mixing up experience and behaviour. 3. Thinking all behaviour is visible. 4. Leaving out "systematic/scientific". 5. No examples.

Quick recall

  1. Three areas of study? 2. Visible behaviour? 3. Internal behaviour? 4. Private states? 5. How studied?

Answers: 1) Mental processes, experiences, behaviour. 2) Overt. 3) Covert. 4) Experiences. 5) Scientific methods.
